title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Abhinav Prem, Matthew Yu
abstract: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.
summary: This theoretical work develops a comprehensive framework to classify mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D by mapping them onto braided fusion 2-categories. By modeling the effect of decoherence on pure-state systems, the authors demonstrate that these mathematical structures govern the physical realization of exotic topological phases, particularly those exhibiting intrinsic mixed-state characteristics.
main_problem: The paper aims to systematically classify and realize mixed-state topological orders (mTOs) in (3+1)D, distinguishing them from pure-state orders by analyzing the role of decoherence and higher-form symmetries.
main_result: Every braided fusion 2-category can be realized as the topological operator category of a (3+1)D mTO via a general construction involving decoherence and gauging. Intrinsically mixed-state orders (imTOs) are characterized by specific anomalous symmetries.
method: The authors employ advanced mathematical tools, relating the data of braided fusion 2-categories to physical symmetries and anomalies, and modeling the process via decoherence channels applied to parent pure-state theories.
model_or_system: The focus is on (3+1)D mixed-state topological orders, exemplified by applying decoherence channels to the fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code Hamiltonian. The mathematical framework utilizes braided fusion 2-categories to encode the topological structure.
key_observables: Strong higher-form symmetries, their anomalies (e.g., 't Hooft anomaly), and the failure of two-way channel connectivity to a pure state.
important_parameters: The dimensionality (3+1)D is crucial, as the authors highlight novel mechanisms absent in (2+1)D, such as gravitational anomalies.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on bosonic theories, and the classification relies on the mathematical structure of braided fusion 2-categories, which is a generalization beyond standard (2+1)D models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the vertex and plaquette terms of the (3+1)D fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code Hamiltonian and define the operators used in the decoherence process.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the mathematical structure of braided fusion 2-categories, generalizing classification tools from (2+1)D to (3+1)D, and finally applying these tools to model the physical process of decoherence to generate mTOs.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework connecting abstract category theory (braided fusion 2-categories) to concrete physical phenomena like decoherence and emergent symmetries in higher-dimensional quantum matter.
